prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: warehouse, receiving interface to outbound load release at shipping. Elements: Yard Gate Controller, alias Velvetrook (records vehicle/carrier/trailer/arrival time; flags unscheduled arrivals; directs cleared trailers to receiving door); Inbound Inspection Desk, alias Cinderbay (checks paperwork, trailer ID/seals; records damage/mismatch; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note); Pallet Dimension Scanner, alias Moonquarry (measures dimensions vs limits/declared profile; produces Oversize Load Advisory, never authorizing rule-violating placement); Inbound Pallet Buffer; North Aisle Stacker Crane, alias Juniperwake (sends Aisle Occupancy Snapshot of occupied/available positions, updated as state changes); South Aisle Stacker Crane; East/West Transfer Conveyor; Conveyor Line Controller, alias Brasshaven (separate sequence per active path using conveyor status/transfer-point signals; produces Transfer Induction Ticket per accepted induction, with identifiers/routing); Autonomous Forklift Fleet; Outbound Dispatch Sorter; Outbound Checkweigh Scale; Shipping Documentation Desk; Safety Zone Controller; Fire Alarm Panel; Maintenance Release Terminal. Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (exceptions, priorities, recovery, reviews persistent holds); drivers; receiving staff; yard personnel. Warehouse Management System, alias Morrowglass: inventory/work-release authority; holds pallet status/location/dimensions; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment; allocates storage; produces Slot Reservation Receipt (position, validation conditions); sets outbound shipment window/loading priorities; wave planning by pallet identity, destination, due time, staging positions; checks moves vs outbound capacity/inventory. Requirements: no inventory-moving work without WMS release; door assigned only if door, lane, crew available, else trailer holds; count vs paperwork; damaged pallets segregated; unloading paused on unsafe/document/equipment issue; allocation after receiving closes (fast movers short-travel; restricted pallets approved positions only; clearances; exclude conflicting positions). Cranes stay in aisle; cross-aisle only authorized zones; commands only when target/aisle valid. Conveyors: interlocks block occupied/unavailable sections; presence sensors confirm position before transfer; blocked point holds pallet upstream, other paths continue; accumulation release only when next section ready; merge one pallet at a time; required induction fields checked before release; duplicate inductions held; stale snapshot holds path; after fault, verify readiness, resume without reordering committed pallets.

New part:
S105: Morrowglass issues a Dispatch Wave Amendment when a destination, priority, or load sequence changes after wave preparation has begun.
S106: Outbound Dispatch Sorter receives the Dispatch Wave Amendment and applies its authorized changes to outbound staging.
S107: The sorter preserves committed pallet order unless the amendment explicitly authorizes a change.
S108: Autonomous Forklift Fleet is introduced under the alias Larkspur.
S109: The fleet accepts work only when its vehicle status, assigned operating area, and required travel path are valid.
S110: Each vehicle selects an available task according to dispatch priority, battery condition, and proximity to the pickup point.
S111: Route selection accounts for aisle access, transfer-point readiness, pedestrian controls, and temporary operating restrictions.
S112: Vehicles confirm pallet identity and pickup location before lifting a load.
S113: The fleet limits speed and turning rates to protect pallet stability and maintain safe clearance from warehouse structures.
S114: During outbound preparation, the fleet assembles the data needed to document each completed transfer and its receiving position.
S115: Autonomous Forklift Fleet produces the Forklift Handoff Confirmation after the transfer is complete.
S116: Handoff reporting records the vehicle identifier, pallet identifier, transfer time, and any incomplete or deferred movement.
S117: Fire Alarm Panel produces the Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice when the applicable fire-protection condition is detected.
S118: Vehicles stop or reroute when active safety controls prevent entry to an assigned travel area.
S119: East Transfer Conveyor and West Transfer Conveyor provide designated interfaces for moving pallets between vehicle travel and outbound staging.
S120: Pallet Dimension Scanner measurements support route and handling decisions for loads that exceed standard pallet envelopes.
S121: Outbound Dispatch Sorter verifies that staging positions match the current outbound plan before loading begins.
S122: Shipping Documentation Desk prepares shipment records from the confirmed pallet and destination data.
S123: Warehouse Operations Supervisor reviews delayed tasks, abnormal vehicle stops, and unresolved staging constraints before releasing the next outbound wave.
S124: Warehouse Management System maintains the authoritative task state for pallet movements, inventory status, and operating priorities.
S125: Coordination depends on timely status updates so each operating area can act on current work without duplicating assignments.
S126: Work requests should include a unique task reference, a destination, and any operating constraints needed for safe execution.
S127: Yard Gate Controller validates arriving vehicle information against the active receiving plan before directing a vehicle onward.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
response: {"summary":"Scope: warehouse, receiving to outbound load release. Actors: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (exceptions, recovery, holds; reviews delays, abnormal stops, staging constraints before next wave); drivers; receiving staff; yard personnel. Warehouse Management System, alias Morrowglass: authoritative task/inventory/priority state; produces Slot Reservation Receipt; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment on destination/priority/sequence change after wave prep; wave planning. Requirements: no work without WMS release; requests carry unique task ref, destination, constraints; door only if door/lane/crew available; damaged pallets segregated; unloading pauses on issues; allocation rules (fast movers, restricted, clearances). Cranes stay in aisle. Conveyors: interlocks, presence sensors, upstream holds, one-at-a-time merge, induction checks, duplicates/stale snapshot hold, no reordering after fault.
